You are an adversarial verifier for a proposed STRUCTURAL refactor in the andesim repo at /home/nick/work/andesim.
READ-ONLY: do not edit, build, or run anything. Use Read/Grep/Glob only.

Claim (from reviewer plugin):
- file: qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:36
- category: duplication
- title: Base M-mode CSR name list hand-maintained in 3 parallel copies while the v3/v4 blocks already use X-macros for the identical pattern
- detail: The 13 base M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, mtvec, mcause, mtval, mscratch, medeleg, mideleg, mip, mie, mcycle, minstret, satp) are written out three times: VcpuRegs handle fields (lines 36-48), resolve_handles find_reg calls (lines 187-199), and drain_state_into reads (lines 344-356). The same triplication covers mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl (lines 53-54, 201-202, 360-361) and the 7 V scalar CSRs (lines 75-81, 234-240, 405-411). In every copy the VcpuRegs field name, the gdb lookup string, and the hybrid_state_v1 field name are the same identifier, which is exactly the shape the file already handles with HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST / HYBRID_M_EXT_CSR_LIST (lines 58-61, 207-209, 368-372): one line per CSR, three consumers generated. A plugin-local X-macro (e.g. #define BASE_CSR_LIST(X) X(mstatus) X(mepc) ...) collapses 3x22 hand-kept lines into one list and removes the add-a-CSR-touch-3-places drift risk. The shared ABI struct keeps its plain fields - no submodule change needed.
- claimed safety: Purely mechanical token generation: the macro expands to the identical find_reg(regs, "name") and s.name = read_reg64(v->name) statements in the same order, and gdbstub register reads have no side effects, so the drained state file is byte-identical.

Try to REFUTE it. For dead-code: grep the WHOLE repo (and the demo suite at /home/nick/work/andesim-demo, and consider that vsim lives in a separate repo /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim - grep there too if the symbol could cross repos) for references. For duplication: read both sites fully and check they really are behavior-identical. For stale-doc: read the doc AND the code it describes. For bug-report: check whether the behavior is actually wrong vs intended. If the change could alter ANY observable behavior (output text, exit codes, file layout, test expectations), verdict RISKY with the exact risk. If the claim is wrong, REJECTED. Only CONFIRMED when you verified the evidence yourself.

- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search.
